program.name: Phase 5 Customer Onboarding
program.description: Let a real person use Keki: the Cognito hosted-UI sign-in handshake the infrastructure was provisioned for in Phase 1 and never used, first-time profile completion, and a parent's ability to add their own children. /auth/sign-in has said "arrives in Phase 2" through three shipped phases, and addChild has been a stub since Phase 1 in a product that sells classes for children.

technology.oauthFlow: Authorization code with PKCE against the Cognito hosted UI; public client with no secret, since the browser initiates the redirect
technology.sessionLifetime: Refresh token in its own httpOnly cookie, exchanged near id-token expiry — a one-hour hard session drops customers mid-checkout
technology.socialLogin: Out of scope; each provider is its own configuration, consent screen, and account-linking problem
technology.profileCompletion: A dedicated /auth/complete-profile step rather than silent provisioning on callback, because provisionCustomerProfile needs a real name
technology.childDateOfBirth: Required — children.date_of_birth is notNull and age decides which class a child belongs in
technology.adminCustomers: Read-only lookup; staff editing a household is a larger second question
technology.demoSignIn: Retained. Every demo has gone through it, it is double-gated, and the e2e fixtures do not use Cognito either
technology.cookieContract: The id-token cookie name and shape must not change — the existing Playwright session fixtures set the same cookie

successCriteria.description: /auth/sign-in redirects to the Cognito hosted UI with a correctly-formed authorization URL carrying client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, and state.
The PKCE verifier and state are stored in httpOnly cookies that survive the redirect round trip.
/auth/callback exchanges an authorization code for tokens and sets the id-token cookie under its existing name and shape.
A callback whose state does not match the cookie is refused before any token exchange.
After callback, the user is returned to the next path they were originally denied.
A session whose id token is near expiry is refreshed without the user signing in again.
/auth/sign-out clears the session cookies and redirects through Cognito's logout endpoint.
A signed-in user with no customers row is sent to /auth/complete-profile.
Completing the profile creates the customer and household, and returns the user to where they were going.
Profile completion is idempotent: submitting twice does not create a second household.
A customer can add a child with a first name, last name, and date of birth.
A child is always added to the caller's own household, never one supplied in the payload.
A future date of birth is refused.
A customer can rename their household.
A newly added child appears as a bookable participant on the class booking flow.
/admin/customers finds a household by customer email or name and shows its members, children, and recent orders.
The existing Playwright session fixtures still work unchanged — the cookie contract did not move.
Playwright covers the journey: complete a profile, add a child, and book that child into a class.

packages.name: auth
packages.description: Gains the OAuth handshake: buildAuthorizationUrl, exchangeCodeForTokens, refreshSession, buildSignOutUrl, and PKCE challenge generation. Stays a library with no Next.js imports so the kiosk surface can reuse it.

packages.name: contracts
packages.description: Input schemas for profile completion, addChild, and household rename, plus the OAuth handshake types (authorization request, token response, state/verifier pair).

packages.name: customer-core
packages.description: addChild and updateHousehold stop rejecting with NotImplementedInPhase1 — its first write paths since Phase 1.

packages.name: infra
packages.description: The Cognito client gains authorization-code flow with PKCE, per-stage callback and logout URLs, and openid/email/profile scopes. The hosted-UI domain, provisioned in Phase 1 and never consumed, becomes an output the app uses.

packages.name: web
packages.description: /auth/sign-in, /auth/callback, /auth/sign-out, /auth/complete-profile, an editable /account, and /admin/customers — the last admin placeholder.

packages.name: ui
packages.description: Presentational additions for the profile and child forms, reusing FormField and EmptyState.

workstreams.name: Contracts: profile, child, and household schemas; OAuth handshake types
Infrastructure: Cognito OAuth client configuration and hosted-UI outputs
@keki/auth: authorization URL, code exchange, refresh, sign-out
/account: add a child and rename the household

outOfScope: Social login, and any external identity provider
MFA, and customizing Cognito's password-reset or email-verification screens
Editing or deleting a child once added
Waivers, play passes, and refunds — still stubs, still out
Account deletion, data export, and other privacy-request tooling
Email change, which is an identity change and belongs with account recovery
